{{Short description|Soviet mathematician}}
'''Suren Yurievich Arakelov''' ({{langx|ru|Суре́н Ю́рьевич Араке́лов}}, {{langx|hy|Սուրեն Յուրիի Առաքելով}}) (born October 16, 1947 in [[Kharkiv]]) is a Soviet mathematician of Armenian descent known for developing [[Arakelov theory]].

== Biography ==
From 1965 onwards Arakelov attended the Mathematics department of [[Moscow State University]], where he graduated in 1971.

In 1974, Arakelov received his [[candidate of sciences]] degree from the [[Steklov Institute of Mathematics|Steklov Institute]] in [[Moscow]], under the supervision of [[Igor Shafarevich]]. He then worked as a junior researcher at the [[Gubkin Russian State University of Oil and Gas]] in Moscow until 1979. He did protest against arrest of [[Alexander Solzhenitsyn]], and was arrested and committed to a mental hospital.<ref>{{cite web |title=What happened to Suren Arakelov? |url=https://mathoverflow.net/a/314602/6818 |website=Mathoverflow}}</ref> Then he stopped his research activity to pursue other life goals. As of 2014 he lives in Moscow with his wife and children.

== Arakelov theory ==
{{main|Arakelov theory}}

[[Arakelov theory]] was exploited  by [[Paul Vojta]] to give a new proof of the [[Mordell conjecture]] and by [[Gerd Faltings]] in his proof of Lang's generalization of the [[Mordell conjecture]].
